title: Bus to Atlantic City: whisky and twenty-five hamburgers
summary: On the way to an Atlantic City gig, Waller passed out bottles, stopped a truck for supplies, and had the bus halt at a roadside stand where he ate about 25 hamburgers.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: The Fats Fats Waller. And he's a tremendous personality so we had another gig. We go down to Atlantic City and it's the first time the musicians are on time. Musicians are never on time, you know. Guys I know ain't never on time but sometimes

it happens. It happened this day. So we get in the bus, you know, start to his house, get in the bus and we make it. So I say, Fats, I mean where you going. He said, Joe, don't worry, just sit in the bus. And, Stan, pretty soon around the corner swooped a great big truck, came swooping around the corner and he jumped out of the truck. He says, Hey, Fats, man, I'm sorry but I got caught in the traffic. He said, don't you worry about it, don't you worry about it at all. So he bought some things in there. He had cases, you know. He must have something, Joe. What she said, what she said so he paid the guy off so there were some more transactions going on and being the nosy I said, what the hell is going on. I want to go, you know, hired from these union rules and all that kind of thing, you know. So the cat says, this is all for me. He said, yeah, man, this is all. He said, thank you, Fats. He give a hell of a tip, you know. So we get on the bus and we ride to Atlantic City. So, he had showboat ideas. You've got to have. A guy's got to show his strength. So he passes out the bottles. Here's one for you, here's/for you. So the cat sitting next to you might have been a cat like Herman Autrey, he says, man, don't tell him you don't drink. I said, take the bottle. Finally he said, one for you and I said, thank you, Fats. Now we get to a roadside stop.
Were you not drinking then because of your stomach?
I didn't care that much about drinking. I drank a little beer, wine. I guess it was because of my stomach. I
drank some good whisky when I was a boy from the vines or grandmother would make, them kind of things, had a little cold or something like that. I got a cold, said, give him a drink.
I wondered if you were off the sauce at that time because of your stomach?

It could have been. No, it wasn't because of my stomach. I didn't even drink. I didn't care that much about it, you know. Look how much money I would have saved if I had stopped drinking now. Wouldn't that be something. So, anyhow I certainly enjoy it. I think it's a necessary thing at certain times.

So, we're on the way to Atlantic City. So he says to the bus driver, comes to a little roadside stand, so he says, hey, bus driver. He say, yeah, Fats, what do you want. Stop over there. Crazy. He drives up in there, little place, drives up in there and they have hamburgers, chicken, onions, potatoes and them kind of things. So he says, you guys order what you want. So we ordered. I had two or three. So people are amazed that all these things are happening right here. They didn't expect anything like that. So what the hell, they're all gone. So Fats thought he was different. And we're all hungry and didn't know it. So I think we all had around two or three apiece. A pretty big band around 12 to 13 people, something like that. So she filled up the grills automatically

again. So nobody wanted any more. So she had around 12 or 25 hamburgers so the boss was standing looking over her shoulder so nobody wanted anything. So she said, what am I going to do with these. "Just put them in a bag, baby. I'll take them." So he took them. On the way to Atlantic City, Stan, he ate, I would say, 25 hamburgers and he drank his whisky on the way down. I got stomach trouble and this is the damnedest thing I've ever seen in my life. So somehow we had ...
Funny though. Amazing that his constitution stood up to it as long as it did.
